vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-tasks
Version: 1.0.9

The skill bundle provides standard documentation and instructions for an AI agent to manage Google Tasks via the 'gws' CLI tool. The content in SKILL.md describes legitimate CRUD operations (list, insert, update, delete) for task lists and tasks, aligns with the stated purpose, and contains no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection attacks.

llm.summary: The skill's actions (calling the gws CLI to manage Google Tasks) match its description, but it defers authentication and security rules to an external ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (not provided) which could request broad Google credentials or scopes — this unresolved dependency makes the package ambiguous.

dimensions.detail: Name/description and required binary ('gws') align: the skill is an instruction-only wrapper that runs 'gws tasks ...' to manage Google Tasks. No unrelated binaries, env vars, or install steps are present.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md's runtime instructions are limited to using the 'gws' CLI for tasklist/task operations, which is appropriate. However the file explicitly requires reading a separate ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules. That external file is not included here, so we cannot confirm what credentials, scopes, or file reads the skill will rely on or instruct the agent to perform.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. This minimizes risk because nothing is downloaded or written by the skill itself. The only runtime requirement is an existing 'gws' binary, which the user must supply.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: This skill declares no required env vars or credentials (primaryEnv none), which is consistent for an instruction-only wrapper. But because auth is delegated to an external shared SKILL.md or to the 'gws' CLI configuration, the actual credential needs (OAuth tokens, service account JSON, or other Google credentials) are unknown and may be broader than necessary — inspect the referenced shared file and your gws config before use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills. It is user-invocable and permits autonomous model invocation (the platform default). No additional persistence or privileged system configuration is declared.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling this skill: (1) Inspect the referenced ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (or run 'gws generate-skills' only after reviewing its template) to see exactly how authentication is performed and what credentials or scopes are requested. That file may request OAuth tokens, service-account JSON, or instructions that store tokens — ensure scopes are limited to Tasks rather than broad Workspace admin scopes. (2) Verify the 'gws' CLI binary you will use is from a reputable source and review its configuration (~/.config or gcloud auth state) so it doesn't carry unrelated permissions. (3) Because this skill is instruction-only, it won’t itself download code, but the actual risk depends on the external auth setup; do not supply broad or admin Google credentials unless you understand and accept the scope. (4) If you need higher assurance, obtain the missing shared SKILL.md and confirm it only requests minimal, task-related scopes and does not instruct reading unrelated local files.
